newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks jump to new high for calendar year.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks jump to new high for calendar year.

text.p: Tokyo stocks jumped to a new high for the calendar year shortly after opening on Friday.
Brokers said activity related to settlement of June futures, purchases by investors inspired by a weaker yen and strength in the U.S. markets overnight lifted the indices.
As of 0010 GMT, the Nikkei 225 average was up 181.81 points, or 0.88 percent, at 20,746.27.
High-tech laggards edged higher, with Toshiba Corp rising one yen to stand at 752.

"The stable yen is definitely helping, but with the Denver G7 summit coming up and uncertainties over currencies, investors are opting for second-in-line high-tech shares rather than the big names," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said.
Sony Corp was slightly weak, down 10 yen at 9,880.
Banks rallied for the second consecutive day as investors bought back the shares they sold off earlier in the year amidst fears over the health of Japan's financial sector.
Sakura Bank Ltd climbed 33 yen to stand at 828.
It was the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse at 9.46 million shares.
Shares of Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd jumped 120 yen or 6.24 percent to 1,250 yen, becoming the largest percentage gainer on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
"Sumitomo Trust's shares were sold off heavily recently due to worries over the bank's issuance of bonds, and short-covering emerged," a broker at a medium-sized brokerage said.
Last week, Sumitomo Trust set terms for 100 billion yen worth of convertible bonds via an overseas unit.

By sector, banks, railway/bus, securities, transport equipment and electric power headed the list of gainers. Mining, sea transport, oil, pulp/paper and precision instruments were at the top of the decliners list.
The TOPIX index was up 11.79 points or 0.77 percent at 1,538.24. The Nikkei 300 rose 2.59 points or 0.88 percent to 297.22.
